Re-Horakhty is the sun that is also a hawk and a king. Each night his barque runs a gauntlet. Each morning is not guaranteed; it is a successful shift.

Clerics of Re keep watches. Daylight is a sacrament. They are terrible people to plan a coup with at noon and excellent people to have when the dark has a name.
worship: Face the sunrise. Do not sleep through a dawn you promised to watch.
hooks: The sun stalled at noon for a count of thirty. Something bit the barque. He wants a crew.
A false sun-disk is being worshipped in a quarry. The real dawn is arriving late there.

name: Selûne
aka: The Moonmaiden, She Who Guides, Our Lady of Silver
symbol: A pair of female eyes surrounded by seven silver stars, or a crescent moon
look: A woman of changing age in silver-white, moon-pale hair, a crescent at her brow, standing on a balcony over a night harbor. Fully clothed. Kind, not fragile. Stars, not glare.
blurb: The moon as a lantern for people who have to walk at night.
text:
Selûne is Shar's sister and opposite. Where Shar wants the dark to be empty, Selûne wants it to be navigable. Sailors, lycanthropes who are trying, and anyone lost on the Coast Way keep her.

In Baldur's Gate her house is a lighthouse of a church. Her clerics heal, guide, and feud with Sharrans in ways the city pretends not to see.

At the table she is a night that helps. A moonlit path. A wolf that did not bite. A dream that is a map.
worship: Walk by moonlight once without a torch. Help someone find the shore. Do not hide from your own night.
hooks: The moon over the harbor went black for an hour and no one in the Upper City noticed. The Lower City did. Selûne's priestess is already packing.
A werewolf in a Selûne shrine wants to be cured before the next full moon. Shar's people have the same appointment.

name: Set
aka: Of the red land, the storm, the necessary outsider
symbol: The set-animal, or a was-sceptre on red sand
look: A powerful man with the mysterious set-animal head (long snout, squared ears), red-and-white desert armour-linen, was-sceptre, a sandstorm wall behind him. Alien, clothed, not gore.
blurb: Desert, storm, and the violence that sometimes holds the barque together. He is a murderer in the old story and a defender in the next chapter.
text:
Set killed Osiris and also stands on the sun-barque to fight Apep. He is the god of foreigners, of necessary force, of the land that will not be farmed. Tables can play him as a villain or as the ugly ally.

Clerics of Set are desert guides, storm-callers, and political knives. They are not welcome at every feast. They are welcome at every sandstorm.
worship: Red beer, a storm-prayer, an honest admission of envy. Do not pretend you are Osiris if you are Set.
hooks: A sandstorm has a shape and a grudge. Set will call it off for a service against Apep's cult.
A foreign company has taken a quarry in his name without asking the desert. The stone is screaming when cut.

name: Shar
aka: Mistress of the Night, Lady of Loss, Nightsinger
symbol: A black disk with a purple border, or a circle of darkness inside a circle
look: A pale, beautiful woman in structured black and deep purple, a void-disk at her throat, eyes that do not reflect the candles. Fully clothed. A windowless chapel, one black candle.
blurb: Loss as a sacrament. Forgetfulness as mercy she will charge for.
text:
Shar is the night with the lanterns taken away. She is Selûne's twin and the older wound. Baldur's Gate has always had Sharrans: grief-cults, spy-rings, people who would rather not remember a name.

A cleric of Shar at the table offers to take a memory. That is not a metaphor. The price is real and the hole it leaves is useful to her.

She is patient. Her plots are the ones that were already running when the party arrived. If a house has no mirrors, ask why.
worship: A secret kept. A light put out on purpose. Do not pray in moonlight. She is the dark between the stars, not the stars.
hooks: A whole street forgot the same man. His bills still arrive. Shar's disk was painted on his door from the inside.
A Sharran will fund the party's job if they retrieve a song that makes listeners forget the last hour. The song is already in a bard's head.

name: Sif
aka: Of the golden hair, the harvest that is a marriage
symbol: A sheaf of gold hair, or a sword laid in grain
look: A composed woman with impossibly gold hair, in a green gown, a field of ripe grain, a sword at rest. Fully clothed, northern, warm.
blurb: The field and the household of thunder. She is plenty, and the reminder that a cruel joke can still be paid for in gold.
text:
Sif's hair was cut as a prank and replaced with gold that grows. She is the harvest you can see from the hall. She is also Thor's match, which means her clerics are not fragile.

A blight on wheat in her country is a crime. Plant growth, hero's feast. A barber-joke in a temple will be expensive.
worship: A braid of the first ripe grain. Do not cut what you cannot replace.
hooks: A whole village woke shorn. Their grain is dying in the same pattern as the missing hair.
Gold hair in a river is tangling mill-wheels. Sif wants the prankster, not a funeral.

name: Silvanus
aka: Of the treeline, horned watcher of the wild wood
symbol: A summer oak, or a wooden mallet
look: A bearded woodland god in a cloak of leaves and bark, antlers modest, a mallet of living wood. Deep forest, no gore, fully covered.
blurb: The forest as a person who was there first. Roads are a guest. Farms are a negotiation.
text:
This Silvanus is the Celtic wood, not a city cult. He is the treeline that does not like being straightened. His mallet is for fence-posts you should not have driven.

Clerics of Silvanus speak for trees that cannot hire lawyers. A logging camp that skipped the offering loses tools in the night. A party that sleeps on roots without asking wakes with sap in their hair and a debt.
worship: Leave the first cut of timber at the stump. Hunt what you eat. Do not map a grove for a mill.
hooks: A Roman-style road is being driven through an oak that has a name. The surveyors are vanishing one peg at a time.
A dryad is not the problem. Silvanus is, and he wants the mill-wheel returned to being a tree.

name: Silvanus
aka: Oak Father, the Forest Father, Treefather
symbol: A green oak leaf, a summer oak, or a wooden staff in leaf
look: A huge, oak-bearded man in living bark and leaf-cloak, staff rooted to the earth, eyes like a canopy. The city is small behind him. Clothed in the forest itself.
blurb: The wild that does not negotiate. Balance, including the kind that eats farms.
text:
This is the Silvanus of the Sword Coast woods, not the old Celtic name on another page. He is the oak that was here before Baldur's Gate and will be here after, if the Gate is not careful.

His druids dislike cities. They will still walk into one if a river is being killed. A cleric of Silvanus at the table is weather, beasts, and a refusal to pave.

He is not sweet. A wolf pack is his choir. A blighted field may be a correction.
worship: Plant what you cut. Do not name a tree after a king. Blood in the soil is a last resort, not a fertilizer plan.
hooks: The oak in the Wide is older than the city and has started shedding leaves in the wrong season. Silvanus wants a conversation under it at midnight.
A logging charter for the Cloakwood has a forged seal. The trees have already started the trial.

name: Skadi
aka: Of the ski, the bow, the mountain that married the sea and went home
symbol: A ski and a bow, or a wolf on a peak
look: A tall huntress on skis, fur-lined coat and trousers, bow, a high white mountain, a distant unhappy harbour far below. Fully clothed, winter, independent.
blurb: Winter hunting and the right to leave a marriage that was the wrong country.
text:
Skadi came out of the mountains to demand weregild with her boots on. She married the sea and missed the wolves. She went home. That is a complete theology of knowing where you can live.

Clerics of Skadi are hunters and divorce-lawyers of the ice. Pass without trace in snow. A forced marriage in her hearing is a combat encounter.
worship: A clean hunt in the high snow. Do not make someone live where they cannot breathe.
hooks: A sea-lord is keeping a mountain bride in a harbour house. The wolves are in the street.
An avalanche opened a hall of skis and bows. Skadi wants them used, not sold.

name: Sobek
aka: Of the crocodile, the river's appetite, the army at the water
symbol: A crocodile, or a plumed crocodile-crown
look: A crocodile-headed warrior in scale-linen and a tall plumed crown, standing in a lotus marsh, army banners on the far bank. Powerful, clothed, river-gold light.
blurb: The river as a mouth that also waters the fields. He is strength, the army, and a very honest hunger.
text:
Sobek is not subtle. He is the crocodile that is also a king. Fayum kept him because the water that feeds you can also take you, and it is better if that has a priest.

Clerics of Sobek are marines and irrigation tyrants. Control water. A party that dumps poison in a river has declared war on a crocodile cult, which is a specific kind of mistake.
worship: Meat in the water, given, not stolen from a trap. Do not boast you 'tamed' a crocodile.
hooks: Crocodiles have left the water and are sitting on a courthouse. Sobek wants a drowned law rewritten.
A dam is starving his marsh. The army that built it is losing men at night, one at a time, to something patient.

name: Sune
aka: Firehair, Lady Firehair, goddess of love and beauty
symbol: A face of a red-haired woman, or a rose in flame-gold
look: A stunning red-gold-haired woman in elegant rose-red silk, a single perfect rose, a painter's warmth, laughing as if the room improved. Fully clothed, glamorous, not a pin-up.
blurb: Beauty as a duty to the world. Love as a risk she still recommends.
text:
Sune is the reason Baldur's Gate has fountains that are nicer than they need to be. Her temples teach that making a place lovely is not vanity. It is resistance to despair.

A cleric of Sune will heal a scar if you want it gone and leave it if it is a story you are proud of. They dislike ugliness that is cruel, not ugliness that is honest.

At the table she is charm with a spine. Her people will walk into a tyrant's hall looking like a festival and refuse to be seated last.
worship: Make something beautiful today. Tell someone they are. Do not use beauty as a knife unless the other person brought a knife first.
hooks: A Sune shrine's mirror shows a party member as they could be if they forgave one person. The shrine wants that person found.
Someone is throwing acid on public art. Sune's priestess will pay in healing and introductions.

name: Surtur
aka: Of the fire that waits at the south end of the story
symbol: A flaming sword taller than a man, or a black fire-crown
look: A gigantic fire-giant king in black-and-gold armour, a sword of fire, a gate of heat behind him, no burning people, apocalyptic forge-light. Clothed in armour, monumental.
blurb: The fire at the end of the world, currently employed as a king of Muspelheim. He is patient. He is not kind.
text:
Surtur is the scheduled fire. Cults that hurry him are fools; cults that ignore him are also fools. He is a lawful end, not a riot.

True clerics of Surtur are rare and alarming. Fireball is not a personality. A table that wants a slow apocalypse antagonist can give him a priest who thinks they are doing maintenance.
worship: A flame that has never cooked a meal. Do not start a fire you cannot name the purpose of.
hooks: A sword in a glacier is steaming. Surtur wants it left until the story says otherwise. Someone is digging.
A fire-cult is trying to skip to the last chapter. The giants are embarrassed, which is worse than angry.

name: Talona
aka: Lady of Poison, Mistress of Disease, She of the Deadly Kiss
symbol: Three amber teardrops on a purple triangle, or a vial and a thorn
look: A thin woman in layered green-black veils and gloves, a physician's satchel of sealed vials, a triangle-mark at her throat. Fully clothed. A clean, wrong infirmary. No rotting bodies.
blurb: Plague as a sermon. Poison as a signature.
text:
Talona is the cough that becomes a street. Baldur's Gate has had her summers. Her cult travels with caravans and with doctors who smile too much.

A cleric of Talona at the table is a biological problem. They may sell the antidote to the thing they started. That is the faith.

Keep her clinical. She is scarier as a pharmacist than as a monster.
worship: A drop in a well is a hymn. A measured dose is a better hymn. Random slaughter bores her.
hooks: The Lower City has a new fever that only hits people who visited one tavern. Talona's triangle is under the bar. The barkeep is already dying and still serving.
A Talonite will halt an outbreak for a relic. The relic is a child's doll that has never been washed.

name: Talos
aka: The Destroyer, Stormlord, the Raging One
symbol: Three lightning bolts from one point, or a storm-gauntlet
look: A towering warrior in storm-dark armor, lightning caught in a raised fist, wreckage of a ship behind him on black water. Clothed in metal. Wrath, not gore.
blurb: Destruction as weather. He is the storm that wants to be thanked.
text:
Talos is the Sword Coast's bad night. Lightning, wreck, riot, the roof coming off. His priests do not build. They wait for a storm and then take credit.

In Baldur's Gate he is a dockside god. Sailors bribe him. The rest of the city pretends the bribe is insurance.

A cleric of Talos at the table is an artillery strike with a holy symbol. They are useful until they are not. Do not stand them next to a library of Gond.
worship: Break something that was too proud. Do it in weather. A whisper in a calm is not his.
hooks: Lightning hit the same warehouse three nights. Talos wants whatever is in the cellar brought outside and named.
A storm-priest is offering to wreck a rival's ship. He will. He will not stop at one ship.

name: Tempus
aka: The Foehammer, Lord of Battles, the Lord of War
symbol: A blazing silver sword on a blood-red field, or a battered war-helm
look: A huge, battle-worn warrior in notched plate, red cloak, a sword that has seen too many wars, standing on a field after the fight. Respect for the fallen. No torture. Clothed in war.
blurb: War as a sacred craft. He loves the fight and hates the clerk who starts one from a desk.
text:
Tempus is the god of the battle, not the massacre. Cowards and butchers offend him. Brave enemies please him. Baldur's Gate keeps him in the barracks and in the heads of people who think a duel still means something.

A cleric of Tempus will bless both sides of a fair war. They will walk away from an assassination and call it what it is.

At the table he is the honest fight. If the party wants a war-god who is not Bane, this is the one.
worship: Fight facing the foe. Spare the beaten. Do not poison a well and call it strategy in his hearing.
hooks: A Tempuran wants the party to referee a gang war so it stays a war and not a slaughter. Both gangs have already cheated.
A sword on an altar will not come free until it has been used in a fight the god considers real. A tavern brawl does not count.

name: The Dagda
aka: The Good God, the All-Father of the Tuatha
symbol: A cauldron, or a club that both slays and restores
look: A huge, rustic chieftain in a short tunic and a cloak of raw wool, belly laughing, club on one shoulder, cauldron steaming at his feet.
blurb: Plenty and ruin share the same table. He feeds armies from a cauldron and knocks down halls with a stick of oak.
text:
The Dagda is not a distant sky. He is the hall that never runs out of stew, and the club that ends a cattle-raid in one blow. Clerics who keep him do not preach. They cook, they fight, they make the next harvest happen.

His cauldron refuses a liar. His harp can order the seasons around a camp like a sergeant. A party that insults hospitality in his country finds the road longer and the rain meaner. A party that feeds strangers finds extra rations in the morning that no one packed.
worship: Shrines are hearths. A cleric of the Dagda blesses a meal, not a statue. Domain work: create food, goodberry, plant growth, and the odd thunderous smash.
hooks: The cauldron in a ruined dun still boils. It will feed the village if someone retrieves the ladle from a fomorian.
His harp was stolen. Until it is played, no one in the valley can sleep or wake on time.

name: The Morrigan
aka: Phantom Queen, of battle and prophecy
symbol: A raven over a ford, or three women as one shadow
look: A dark-haired woman in a cloak of black feathers over a red gown, standing in a shallow ford, a raven on her wrist. Fully clothed, no corpses.
blurb: She is the battle before it starts and the crow after. She offers victory. She does not offer comfort.
text:
The Morrigan is one and three: washer at the ford, queen of phantoms, crow on the shoulder of the dying. She will stand in the river and wash the armour of someone who has not died yet. That is not a riddle. That is a warning.

Her clerics do not soothe. They tell you who will break. A paladin who wants a kind war-god should look elsewhere. A table that wants omens with teeth should keep her close.
worship: Leave meat for crows at a crossing. Do not ask her who wins if you cannot hear the answer.
hooks: She was seen washing a PC's cloak in a stream. She will trade the vision for a service at the next ford.
A king refused her and lost a battle he had already won on paper. His banner is still in the river.

name: Thor
aka: Of the hammer, the storm, the hall-friend of ordinary people
symbol: Mjolnir, a goat, or a thunder-wheel
look: A red-bearded, broad warrior in a simple rich tunic and belt, hammer raised, goats in the storm-light, protecting a farmstead-sized world. Clothed, heroic, not a caricature.
blurb: Thunder that is on your side if you are small and being kicked. He is the most popular god for a reason.
text:
Thor kills giants and drinks with farmers. He is not subtle and he is not cruel. His hammer comes back. His goats come back. The point is that ordinary life is allowed to continue.

Clerics of Thor are the reason a village militia holds. Thunderwave, call lightning. A party that preys on farmers in his country will hear wheels in the sky.
worship: Ale, a goat if you can spare it, a boast you can back. Do not bully a hall.
hooks: Giants are moving a millstone that is actually a hammer-head. Thor wants it thrown, not studied.
A taxman is taking goats 'for the jarl' and the storms have started answering doors.

name: Thoth
aka: Of the ibis, the moon-count, the word that is a number
symbol: An ibis, a baboon, or a scribe's palette
look: An ibis-headed scribe in star-white linen, palette and reed pen, a moon-disk, scrolls in perfect stacks, night-blue temple. Intellectual, clothed, calm.
blurb: Writing, the calendar, and the magic that is just extremely good filing.
text:
Thoth invented letters so the gods could not lie about what they said yesterday. He umpires cosmic disputes. He is why a contract, a spell, and a calendar are cousins.

Clerics of Thoth are scribes. Comprehend languages, identify, legend lore. A party that burns a library in his nome will find they can no longer count past seven until they copy a book by hand.
worship: A true copy. Ink on the altar. Do not sign a blank page in his house.
hooks: Every date in a city is wrong by three days. Thoth wants the stolen calendar-stone.
A spell is misspelled in every book except one. That one is in a crocodile pond. He is not sorry.

name: Thrym
aka: King of the rime-giants, thief of hammers
symbol: A hoar-frost crown, or a stolen hammer-silhouette
look: A massive frost-giant king in rime-crusted mail and furs, a empty hammer-stand beside his throne, aurora over a frozen hall. Clothed, cold, greedy.
blurb: The ice that wants the thunder's tool. He is a bride-price joke that almost worked.
text:
Thrym stole Mjolnir and asked for Freya as the price. The gods sent Thor in a dress. The stories are allowed to be funny and still end in a pile of giants.

Clerics of Thrym are rare outside Jotun cults. They want winter to last and tools to change owners. A stolen magic weapon in a cold dungeon may be a tithe.
worship: A stolen tool laid on ice. Do not pretend to be a bride if you cannot finish the joke.
hooks: A frost-giant wedding is tomorrow. The bride is a problem. The dowry is a legendary weapon.
Every hammer in a town has frozen to the anvil. Thrym wants a conversation about a loan.

name: Tiamat
aka: The Chromatic Dragon, Queen of Evil Dragons, the Dark Queen, the Avaricious
symbol: A five-headed dragon, or five colored gems in a claw
look: A draconic queen in jeweled chromatic scale-mail, a five-colored crown, one claw on a hoard, five ghost-heads of dragon-fire in the smoke above her. Clothed in treasure. Greedy, imperial, not a pin-up.
blurb: Greed with five throats. She wants the hoard, the throne, and the map to the next hoard.
text:
Tiamat is Bahamut's opposite and the reason chromatic dragons have a foreign policy. Her cult in Baldur's Gate is money, dragon-blooded ambitious people, and a rumor of a hidden shrine that smells like a mint.

A cleric of Tiamat at the table will help if the take is large enough. They will eat the take. The contract should be read twice.

She is a lawful evil: hierarchies, tribute, color-coded grudges. Red is not green. Do not mix the books.
worship: Tribute in the correct color. A stolen hoard is a hymn. A shared hoard is a heresy.
hooks: Five colored coins were left on the party's table. Spending them summons a collector. The collector is polite.
A Tiamat cult is funding both sides of a dock war. They want the warehouses empty so a dragon can nest. The dragon is not a metaphor.

name: Torm
aka: The True, the Loyal Fury, Hand of Righteousness
symbol: A gauntlet held upright, or a lion's head on a white field
look: A handsome, earnest warrior in bright plate, lion-cloak, a gauntlet raised in oath, standing before a city gate at morning. Fully clothed. Duty you can like.
blurb: Loyalty as a superpower. Paladins' other favorite, after the one who cries.
text:
Torm is the god of keeping the promise you made when you were still brave. He is popular with the Flaming Fist's better officers and with people who think Baldur's Gate could be a just city if someone insisted.

A cleric of Torm will not abandon the party. That can be inconvenient. They will also not ignore a crime because it is useful.

At the table he is the lawful good that still goes into the sewer. He is not naive. He is stubborn.
worship: Swear with a gauntlet on a table. Then go. Do not leave a post. Do not leave a friend.
hooks: A Tormite just resigned from the Fist for refusing an order. He will tell the party the order if they walk with him to the person it would have hurt.
An upright gauntlet appeared on a door in the Outer City. Behind the door is a child the city forgot. Torm has not.

name: Tyche
aka: Of the city's luck, the wheel that does not apologise
symbol: A rudder, a cornucopia, or a wheel
look: A crowned woman in a mural crown (city walls as a diadem), rudder in one hand, cornucopia in the other, a city behind her. Clothed, civic, slightly smiling.
blurb: Luck as civic infrastructure. She is why one town always catches the fair wind.
text:
Tyche is the fortune of a place, not a dice charm. When she leaves a city, the dice still work and nothing good happens with them. When she stays, even a bad mayor gets a good harvest.

Clerics of Tyche keep a public shrine at the market gate. Bane and bless are both hers. A party that wants 'luck' from her will be asked what they did for the town this week.
worship: A coin in the civic fountain, heads-up. Do not pray for another city's ruin in her hearing.
hooks: The town's luck left in a box on a cart. The cart is three days ahead on the road.
A rival city stole her mural crown from a statue. Birds will not land in either place until it is returned.

name: Tymora
aka: Lady Luck, Our Smiling Lady, the Lady Who Smiles
symbol: A silver coin with her face, or a shining featureless disk
look: A laughing woman in traveling blue and silver, a coin walking across her knuckles, wink ready, a tavern behind her that is having a good night. Fully clothed. Warm, not drunk.
blurb: Good fortune for people willing to roll. She likes a brave bet more than a safe prayer.
text:
Tymora is Beshaba's sister and the reason adventurers toast before a job. Baldur's Gate loves her: gambling houses, sailors, anyone whose plan has a fifty-fifty.

A cleric of Tymora will bless a leap. They will not bless a ledger. If the party never takes a risk, she gets bored and her sister does not.

At the table she is the god of the second chance that still requires you to jump.
worship: Flip a coin and abide. Leave a silver in a fountain. Do not count cards in her house and then ask for a miracle.
hooks: A coin landed on its edge in the Elfsong and has not fallen. Tymora wants a question asked out loud. The answer will be expensive and correct.
Lady Luck's priest will stake the party for a vault job if they let her roll the last die.

name: Tyr
aka: One-handed keeper of the oath, who paid in advance
symbol: A sword, a missing right hand, or a bound wolf's shadow
look: A grave, one-handed war-god in simple mail, right wrist ending cleanly, sword in the left, a great wolf bound in the distance, hall-law light. Clothed, honourable, no gore.
blurb: The oath that costs a hand. He is courage, law, and the bill you knew you would pay.
text:
Tyr put his hand in the wolf's mouth so the binding would hold. He is the god of people who sign knowing the price. Cowards do not keep him long.

Clerics of Tyr are officers and judges. They hate a clever oath that was always a lie. Zone of truth, crusader's mantle. A party that breaks parole in his name will find their own right hands unreliable.
worship: A vow with a witness. Do not swear what you will not pay.
hooks: A bound monster is chewing through a contract. Tyr wants a new witness, living.
A captain lost a hand in a false truce. He wants the truce-maker, and Tyr is already walking with him.

name: Tyr
aka: The Even-Handed, Grimjaws, God of Justice
symbol: A balanced scale resting on a warhammer, or a wounded-but-upright sword
look: A missing-right-hand noble warrior, eye-patch, warhammer in the remaining fist, scales on a chain at his belt, a court-hall that is also a barracks. Clothed, grim, fair.
blurb: Justice that paid in advance. He already gave the hand and the eye. You can give the truth.
text:
This is the Tyr of Baldur's Gate, cousin in spirit to the northern one-hand on another page. He is the court that does not sell. His clergy keep law when the city would rather keep convenience.

A cleric of Tyr at the table will insist on a trial even when a knife would be faster. They are exhausting. They are how a party stays the good side.

He is missing a hand because an oath cost it. Mention that if you want a paladin to sit up straight.
worship: Tell the truth in a hall. Return what was stolen to the person it was stolen from, not to a fence. A maimed oath is still an oath.
hooks: A magistrate of Tyr was found with his scales stuffed with coin. He says he did not do it. The scales still balance. That is the problem.
Tyr's hammer on an altar will not lift for anyone who is lying about why they came. The party has to pick a spokesperson.

name: Uller
aka: Of the yew-bow, the bone-skate, the duel in the snow
symbol: A longbow of yew, or a bone skate
look: A lone hunter on bone skates, yew bow, fur hood, a frozen lake and pine edge, winter dusk. Fully clothed, spare, sharp.
blurb: Archery, duels, and the winter road that is a weapon.
text:
Uller keeps the winter when even Thor is elsewhere. He is the bow, the skate, the single combat on a lake. Oaths sworn on his ring are mean and binding.

Clerics of Uller are archers and duel-seconds. Hail of thorns, hunter's mark. A party that refuses a fair duel in the snow may still have to skate it.
worship: A ring-oath in winter. The first arrow of a hunt left in a tree.
hooks: A frozen lake is a courtroom. Uller wants a champion to skate a lie down.
Every bowstring in a fort has gone slack except one yew. It will only serve a just shot.

name: Umberlee
aka: The Bitch Queen, Queen of the Depths, the Wavemother
symbol: A forked blue-green wave, or a drowning hand and a shark
look: A wrathful sea-queen in kelp-dark silk and foam-white, crown of coral, the harbor storming behind her. Fully clothed in the sea. Beautiful the way a reef is beautiful: you do not grab it.
blurb: The sea as a god who wants to be paid. Drowning is the invoice.
text:
Umberlee has a Water Queen's House on the Baldur's Gate docks because the city is not stupid. Ships leave a cut. Storms still happen. The cut is not a guarantee. It is a maybe.

A cleric of Umberlee at the table is a maritime problem. They can calm a bay. They can also take a person who skipped the tithe.

She is not a metaphor for 'nature.' She is a queen with a temper and a lot of water.
worship: Gold into the harbor. A true fear of the deep. Do not whistle a storm down unless you can put it back.
hooks: A ship refused the Water Queen's cut and arrived anyway. Umberlee wants to know who blessed it. The blessing smells like Selûne.
Bodies have been coming in with the tide, all missing the same offering-coin. Someone is skimming the goddess.

name: Waukeen
aka: Merchant's Friend, Liberty's Maiden, the Golden Lady
symbol: A gold coin with her face, or a pair of scales over a trade-road
look: A prosperous woman in travel-cut gold and green, a ledger and a sample-pouch, a smile that has done this deal before. Fully clothed. A market at peak hour, honest weights in the foreground.
blurb: Trade as a holy road. She wants the caravan through, the contract clear, the coin moving.
text:
Waukeen is why Baldur's Gate has a philosophy of money that is not only greed. Her people bless markets, loans, and the idea that a city is a machine for moving goods.

She has been missing and returned, which the church treats the way a company treats a founder who came back from the dead: carefully.

A cleric of Waukeen at the table will fund a job that increases trade and walk away from one that only burns a rival. They are the party's accountant with a holy symbol.
worship: A fair weight. A paid debt. A coin given to open a road, not to close one.
hooks: A Waukeenar will underwrite the party's expedition if they reopen a trade spur the Zhentarim 'closed.' The spur is a person.
Gold coins in the counting-house have her face on both sides tonight. Spending them is fine. Hoarding them is not.

name: Zeus
aka: King of Olympus, cloud-gatherer
symbol: A fistful of lightning, or an eagle
look: A mature, bearded king in a white himation with a gold border, standing in cloud, a bolt resting in his hand like a sceptre, an eagle at his shoulder. Fully clothed.
blurb: Sky, law, and the right to throw the furniture. He is hospitality and the storm that punishes those who break it.
text:
Zeus keeps the guest-right and the weather. He has a long list of children and a longer list of people who thought a closed door would hide them. At a table he is the reason a host who poisons a guest finds the roof open to rain.

His clerics are judges with a weather problem. They take xenia seriously: bread, salt, a bed, and no knives. Call lightning is not a metaphor.
worship: Offer the first cup of wine to the sky. Protect a guest even if they are inconvenient.
hooks: A guest was murdered under a peace-banner. The next storm will not stop until someone is named.
An eagle will not leave a PC's pack. Zeus wants a message carried to a king who has stopped building guest-houses.
